name: Mesmer
description:
You know what the room needs to believe before you’ve said a word. The mask helps—not because it hides you, exactly, but because it offers everyone present the version of you that makes the situation make sense. You know your technique. You know your approach. What you don’t know yet is whether, when the moment arrives and the performance lands with the weight of inevitability, what fires next will be practiced skill or something harder to explain.

A Mesmer’s power runs through their masks—items that adhere magically to their face once worn, each concealing a randomly selected ability even from its wearer. When a Mesmer performs a technique using Mesmerize, they roll against a hidden threshold; if the roll matches precisely, the hidden ability reveals itself and ignites without cost. If it doesn’t, the performance still has force. Skilled demeanor, careful framing, well-chosen words—these operate on their own terms, with or without magical backing. A Mesmer typically carries several masks, each opening into a different domain: enchantment, illusion, fear. They know roughly what country they’re working in. Whether the spell actually fires is a matter of technique, timing, and something more difficult to predict.

The Mesmer’s edge compounds. Unsettling Presence means each Condition checked on a target adds to the Mesmer’s advantage on the next ability aimed at them—but only while the mask is on, and only while the target has never seen the Mesmer’s real face. That second condition is structural, not incidental. An unmasked Mesmer facing someone who has studied their features is a diminished thing. The mask is not costume. It is the wall between the Mesmer’s full power and its limits, and keeping that wall intact is part of the practice.

What the Mesmer can bring to bear is broad: Charm Person turns hostility into warmth; Suggestion plants a course of action that the target follows as though they arrived at it themselves; Fear turns the Mesmer into the object of a creature’s deepest dread and sends it running. Geas binds a creature to a task for weeks at a time. Doppelgänger deploys a second version of the Mesmer while the original watches through borrowed eyes. The connecting logic is always perception: what the target sees, believes, or dreads, and whether that can be changed before the situation requires something louder. A Mesmer rarely needs to win a fight. They need to ensure the fight never becomes the kind they’d lose.

Play a Mesmer if you want to:

  • Win encounters before they become fights, reshaping what opponents perceive, believe, and fear until the situation has already resolved in your favor.

  • Work through masks—literal and otherwise, keeping your true face hidden and your capabilities unknown, to your targets and sometimes to yourself.

  • Operate at the edge of technique and magic, never quite certain where performance ends and the spell begins, and using that ambiguity as a weapon.

Questions to consider when making a Mesmer:

  • What draws them to the masks—concealment, craft, or the version of themselves the mask makes possible? And is there somewhere the mask comes off, or has the boundary dissolved?

  • How do they relate to the unpredictability of Mesmerize? Are they someone who has cultivated patience for the moment of reveal, or someone who finds it maddening to not be in full control?

  • Have they ever encountered someone who genuinely couldn’t be charmed—who saw through the technique from the first moment? What did that reveal about the Mesmer, and did it stick?

  • Where do they draw the line? Charm is one thing; a compulsion that doesn’t lift for a month is another. Have they used everything available to them, and what did it cost to find out where their limit was?

  • What would it mean to be truly unmasked—not in a fight, but in a life? Is there a self underneath the practice, or has sustained persona made that question unanswerable?

novizio.abilities:
Masked Charlatan, Mesmerize, Social Savvy, Unsettling Presence.

Also choose any two Mesmer's Masks from this mestiere or from one of your home Cultures. You gain one ability chosen at random from each of those masks' domains.
